BillAnalysis_Adjustment.description:
An adjustment that will be applied to any cost row for which one of the rules match.
The first rule to match will determine the cost & usage multipliers to use.
The base cost will be the raw cost of the row, or if any build_on_adjustments are specified, then those adjusted costs will be added in to form the base cost.
The final cost of this adjustment will be the (base_cost * cost_multiplier) + (usage_amount * usage_multiplier)

build_on_adjustments.description:
If none specified, the base cost is simply the raw cost. 
Can also specify one or more of the adjustment names that were defined earlier in the adjustment list, and the base cost will be the net cost after those adjustments are applied.

name.description: Name of the adjustment

rules.description:
List of rules to determine the cost/usage multipliers to apply to a given cost row.
The rules will be evaluated in order until one matches. If none matches, this adjustment is not applied.
The list may contain up to 100 rules.

billing_center_ids.description: IDs of BillingCenters to get cost data for. It is not allowed for any of the BillingCenterIDs to be an ancestor of another specified BillingCenterID.

dimensions.description: The list of supported dimensions by which to roll up the costs.

end_at.description:
Latest timestamp (exclusive) of the costs.
For month granularity: consists of a year and month in YYYY-MM format.
For day granularity: consists of a year, month, and day in YYYY-MM-DD format.
Will be interpreted as UTC, which is used for period boundaries.
No records will be returned on or after this timestamp.

granularity.description:
Indicates which data source to query, having costs already aggregated up to this granularity.
Choosing this granularity wisely can improve performance, as choosing to fetch 1 month of costs with 'month' granularity will be faster than fetching the same 31 days at 'day' granularity.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return. If this limit does not allow all rows to be returned, rowsTruncated:true will be added to the response to indicate the result is incomplete.

metrics.description:
Metrics to return.
When metric 'usage_amount' is requested, dimension 'usage_unit' must be requested
in the dimensions parameter.

period_type.description:
Determines which date column to use for filtering.
 - 'charge_period' (default) filters by ChargePeriodStart/ChargePeriodMonth.
 - 'billing_period' filters by BillingPeriodStart/BillingPeriodMonth.

For V1 orgs, only 'charge_period' is supported. V2 orgs support both 'charge_period' and 'billing_period'. If 'billing_period' is selected but the billing data does not contain Billing Period information, the system will fall back to using ChargePeriod for filtering.

start_at.description:
Earliest timestamp (inclusive) of the returned costs.
For month granularity: consists of a year and month in YYYY-MM format.

Will be interpreted as UTC, which is used for period boundaries.

 - 'billing_period' filters by BillingPeriodStart/BillingPeriodMonth.

For V1 orgs, only 'charge_period' is supported. V2 orgs support both 'charge_period' and 'billing_period'. If 'billing_period' is selected but the billing data does not contain Billing Period information, the system will fall back to using ChargePeriod for filtering.

start_at.description:
Earliest timestamp (inclusive) of the returned costs.
For month granularity: consists of a year and month in YYYY-MM format.
For day granularity: consists of a year, month, and day in YYYY-MM-DD format.
Will be interpreted as UTC, which is used for period boundaries.

Azure Cost & Usage configuration.
AccountType is declared here alongside BillingScope and scope-specific fields.

BillingScope rules (validated in OnboardingCreateRequest):

    - MCA Billing Account: no extra fields required

    - CSP Billing Account: no extra fields required

FinopsBilling_AdjustmentCondition.description:
An adjustment condition, used by adjustment rules and adjustment plan rules.

A rule's condition may be omitted or null, which will match unconditionally.

Otherwise the **"type"** field is required and controls which other fields are required.
The following types are supported in billing adjustment rules:

Type **"dimension_equals"** evaluates whether the specified **"dimension"** contains exactly the specified **"value"**.

```
{"type":"dimension_equals", "dimension":"ProviderName", "value":"AWS"}
```

For rule types _azureReservationReallocation_, _azureSavingsPlanReallocation_, _removeAzureLicenseCosts_, _removeTax_, _reservationReallocation_, _savingsPlanReallocation_, _supportCharge_, _uncompressPricingTiers_, and _volumeDiscounts_, **"dimension"** may only be **"bill_source"**.
For rule types _creditMemo_ and _fixedAmount_, **"dimension"** may be **"SubAccountId"** or **"SubAccountName"**.
For other rule types, **"dimension"** may be any of most [FOCUS columns](https://focus.finops.org/focus-columns),
[Rule-Based Dimensions](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Administration/CreatingRule-BasedDimensions.htm)
defined within your organization (names starting with **rbd\_**),
[Tag Dimensions](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Administration/TagDimensions.htm)
defined within your organization (names starting with **tag\_**),
or a few dimensions Flexera populates for you.

A 'value' specified as an empty string ("") matches dimensions with either a null or an empty string value.

Types **"and"** and **"or"** evaluate whether all or any of the conditions specified in the array **"expressions"** are true.
Type **"not"** evaluates to the opposite of the single condition specified in **"expression"**.

```
{"type":"and", "expressions":[{...}]}
```
```
{"type":"or", "expressions":[{...}]}
```
```
{"type":"not", "expression":{...}}
```

Together types **"and"**, **"or"**, and **"not"** enable complex combinations of other conditions.

dimension.description: The dimension to check the value of. Required for the 'dimension_equals' type.

expressions.description: the expressions that will be AND'd or OR'd together. Required for the 'and' and 'or' types.

type.description: Specifies the condition type, depending on which type is selected, other field(s) will be required.

value.description: The value that the dimension must match. Required for the 'dimension_equals' type.

FinopsBilling_Allocation.description: Defines the allocation strategy and the destinations that receive the reallocated costs.

destinations.description: The destinations that receive the reallocated costs.

type.description: The allocation strategy, and the discriminator for which of a destination's fields carry meaning. equalSplit distributes the pooled cost equally across the destinations. fixedPercentageSplit uses the percentage supplied for each destination, and those percentages must sum to 100. usageBasedProportionalSplit derives each destination's share from that destination's own usage when the bill runs, so the shares are not known at the time a rule is read or written. Further strategies may be added, so consumers must tolerate a value they do not recognize.

FinopsBilling_AllocationDestination.description: A destination that receives a portion of the reallocated costs.

dimensionId.description: Unique identifier of the destination dimension.

dimensionName.description: Human-readable display name of the destination dimension.

percentage.description: The effective percentage of costs allocated to this destination. For equalSplit this is computed by the server as 100/N (where N is the number of destinations) and for fixedPercentageSplit it is the client-supplied value; in both cases all percentages sum to 100. For usageBasedProportionalSplit the effective share is derived from usage at bill run time and is not known when the rule is read, so this field is reported as 0 and carries no meaning -- read "type" to know whether it applies.

value.description: The specific dimension value that receives costs.

FinopsBilling_AllocationDestinationPaylo.description: A destination input used when creating or updating a shared cost rule.

dimensionId.description: Unique identifier of the destination dimension.

percentage.description: The percentage of costs allocated to this destination. Required for fixedPercentageSplit (all percentages must sum to 100). Ignored for equalSplit (the server computes equal shares automatically) and for usageBasedProportionalSplit (shares are derived from usage at bill run time).

value.description: The specific dimension value that receives costs.

FinopsBilling_AllocationPayload.description: Defines the allocation strategy and destination inputs for create/update operations.

destinations.description: The destination inputs that receive the reallocated costs.

type.description: The allocation strategy, and the discriminator for which of a destination's fields are required. equalSplit distributes the pooled cost equally across the destinations. fixedPercentageSplit uses the percentage supplied for each destination, and those percentages must sum to 100. usageBasedProportionalSplit derives each destination's share from that destination's own usage when the bill runs, so the shares are not known at the time a rule is read or written.

dimension.description: Column to filter on. Required when type is "equal" or "substring".

expressions.description: Child filters AND'd or OR'd together. Required when type = "and" or "or". Must contain at least two entries.

substring.description: Case-insensitive substring the dimension must contain. Required when type = "substring".

type.description: Filter node type.

value.description: Exact value the dimension must equal. Required when type = "equal".

yearMonth.description: Year-month in YYYYMM (audit grain is monthly)

periodType.description: Echo of the requested period type (or `chargePeriod` if the request omitted it).

FinopsBilling_CustomUsageRateSettings.description:
Configure an internally-defined unit price to rewrite select Billed Cost and Effective Cost line items.

Conditions for customUsageRate rules often examine several of the following dimensions:
- **ChargeCategory** or **PricingCategory** to differentiate between usage or discounted pricing
- **ServiceName** or **ServiceCategory** to apply to a service or category
- **SKUId** to differentiate by vendor's SKU
- **CommitmentDiscountId** to apply to selected reservations
- **ResourceId** or **ResourceType** to apply to a resource or set of resources

Tiers allow setting multiple rates by cost bracket.
The total cost captured by the rule's condition is broken up against the bounds of the tiers to calculate marginal usage within each tier.
Each tier's rate is applied to its portion of the usage, and the total replaces the original cost.

If multiple customUsageRate rules apply to the same usage record, the rules are evaluated in succession and may override preceding rules.

rate.description: Rate replaces the decimal cost for each unit of usage matching the condition.

tiers.description: Define tiers. These must be continuous without gaps.

FinopsOnboarding_AzureCspExportDetails.description:
Connecting bill with exports is Recommended.

When ExportDetails are provided, the bill connect will gather billing information using exports set-up by the users.
Otherwise, the bill connect will rely on Azure's Cost Management APIs to gather billing information.

ExportDetails indicates the location of Actual and Amortized cost data exports stored in
Azure Blob Storage and provides option to trigger an export.
Both locations are mandatory if the underlying Azure EA Bill Connect must use exports. The file partitioning must be
enabled while creating an export and granularity must be set to daily. If an export was made on the GUI all you have
to do is to make sure that the *Export Type* is set to *Daily export of month-to-date costs*.

The storage location being provided must contain usage details for all the billing periods which the user is interested in.
If we fail to find the usage data for a given billing period, we assume there was no usage.

Each export must be for a time period of exactly one month. You can verify this by making sure all the folders
saved by the export are formatted as such: YYYYMMDD-YYYYMMDD where the dates are the first and last dates of the month respectively.

For Azure CSP Subscription scope, exportDetails is mandatory.

See [Export set up](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/costs/tutorial-export-acm-data?tabs=azure-portal)
for more details on how to create an export for both Actual and Amortized cost and enable file partitioning.

actualCostExportURL.description: URL of Azure CSP actual cost data which has been set up using an export.

amortizedCostExportURL.description: URL of Azure CSP amortized cost data which has been set up using an export.

enableOOBExports.description: Enable Flexera to trigger Out-of-band (OOB) exports to generate cost data more frequently than once per day.

storageTenantID.description: The Tenant ID of the storage account used for export storage. This can be the same as or different from the Azure CSP tenant

FinopsOnboarding_AzureCspScopeDetailsWit.description:
Scope Details allow users to specify the scope of the configured exports.
The scope can be either a billing account, billing profile, customer tenant, or subscription.
If no scope details are provided, billing account scope is assumed to be the default.
The Billing Profile ID, along with the Billing Account ID, is required to gather billing data for a specific billing profile.
The Customer Tenant ID, along with the Billing Account ID, is required to gather billing data for a specific customer tenant.
For Subscription scope, the Billing Account ID is not available for tier-2 CSPs. Instead, the Subscription ID is used to gather billing data for tier-2 CSP customers.

scopeType.description: The type of the scope. Possible values: "Billing Account", "Billing Profile", "Customer Tenant", "Subscription".

isNameManagedByIDP.description:
Indicates whether this user's name is managed by an
external identity provider (AD/SAML).

When **true**, the org has a SAML IDP configured with both JIT-provisioning and
profile-master enabled. Name edits made via the UI may be overridden on the user's
next SSO login if the AD/SAML attribute mapping still points to different values.

The UI should display a warning to admins when this flag is true before they edit
the user's name, to set expectations about sync behavior.

Note: This is an org-level check. It does not distinguish between federated users
(who sync from AD) and local Okta users in the same org. This is a known MVP
limitation — a future version will perform a per-user check based on the user's
identity provider type.

isNameManagedByIDP.description:
Indicates whether this user's name is managed by an
external identity provider (AD/SAML).

When **true**, the org has a SAML IDP configured with both JIT-provisioning and
profile-master enabled. Name edits made via the UI may be overridden on the user's
next SSO login if the AD/SAML attribute mapping still points to different values.

The UI should display a warning to admins when this flag is true before they edit
the user's name, to set expectations about sync behavior.

Note: This is an org-level check. It does not distinguish between federated users
(who sync from AD) and local Okta users in the same org. This is a known MVP
limitation — a future version will perform a per-user check based on the user's
identity provider type.

orgTagsFilter.description:
Filter expression for targeting organizations by tags for policy application.

### Operators
| Operator | Description | Example |
| -------- | ----------- | ------- |
| co | Contains | tags co 'service:level' |
| eq | Equal | tags eq 'region:us-east' |
| ne | Not Equal | tags ne 'service:level:basic' |

### Usage Notes
* Operators are case-sensitive (lowercase only)
* Combine filters with 'and'/'or'
* Group with parentheses for precedence

### Examples
| Expression | Matches |
| ---------- | ------- |
| tags eq 'service:level:basic' | Organizations with exact tag |
| tags co 'service:level' | Organizations with tags containing substring |
| (tags eq 'region:us-east' or tags eq 'region:us-west') | Organizations in either region |
| (tags eq 'service:level:premium' and tags co 'region:us') | Premium organizations in US regions |

orgTagsFilter.description:
Filter expression for targeting organizations by tags for policy application.

### Operators
| Operator | Description | Example |
| -------- | ----------- | ------- |
| co | Contains | tags co 'service:level' |
| eq | Equal | tags eq 'region:us-east' |
| ne | Not Equal | tags ne 'service:level:basic' |

### Usage Notes
* Operators are case-sensitive (lowercase only)
* Combine filters with 'and'/'or'
* Group with parentheses for precedence

### Examples
| Expression | Matches |
| ---------- | ------- |
| tags eq 'service:level:basic' | Organizations with exact tag |
| tags co 'service:level' | Organizations with tags containing substring |
| (tags eq 'region:us-east' or tags eq 'region:us-west') | Organizations in either region |
| (tags eq 'service:level:premium' and tags co 'region:us') | Premium organizations in US regions |

| sixty          | The metric represents 60 days of data                                                   |

Saas_FlexeraFsmImportjob.description: An object representation of the import job. An import job behaves as a fire and forget object. Once the ImportJob is created, it is immediately placed into ready for processing. The number of concurrent jobs that may be in the running state is ten. The ImportJobs will remain in the ready state until currently running jobs fall below ten. An ImportJob has a maximum runtime of 24 hours. After 24 hours the import job will fall into a failed state.

clients in order to understand the field within the wider context of the domain.

definition is associated to an application which has no appTechnopediaId

Queries the costs stored at the given granularity, filtered by the BillingCenters provided.
This action is nearly identical to `costs/aggregated` except this returns the stored costs unmodified, with no group-by aggregation performed. So it can quickly return results (up to the max row `limit`) even for queries that would otherwise produce a very large response. Additionally, it supports returning the `resource_id` dimension.
For month granularity, the start_at and end_at times are specified in YYYY-MM format, and can cover no more than 24 months. For day granularity, the start_at and end_at times are specified in YYYY-MM-DD format, and can cover no more than 31 days. User must have the 'optima:billing_center:show' privilege on the billing center(s) to make this call.

get.description: Index a list of Credentials using optional filters.

parameters.description:
Optional filter for Credentials.

The following filters are supported:

| Filter | Allowed Operators | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| createdAt | eq le lt ge gt | createdAt ge '2019-08-07T23:59:59Z' |
| id | co eq ne | id eq 'azure-ro' |
| name | co eq ne | name co 'Azure' |
| scheme | eq ne | scheme eq 'api-key' |
| tags._tag-name_ | co eq ne | tags.cloud-provider eq 'Azure' |
| updatedAt | eq le lt ge gt | updatedAt lt '2023-02-01T12:23:34Z' |

### Filter Notes
- Filter parameters may be combined using logical 'and', 'or' operators.
- Filter is a query parameter and must be URL-encoded.

get.description:
Returns a report comparing the budget and forecast to the actual spend.

The response is similar to the rows returned by the `costs/aggregated` API.

Each row represents a specific combination of dimension values and timestamp, and includes the corresponding budget amount, forecast amount, actual spend amount and variance (between forecast and actual).

The API also expects the user to have cost access to the segments in the report. If the budget uses billing center level dimensions, access to each row/segment
is determined by the user's access to costs on the billing center. If the budget doesn't use billing center level dimensions, then the user is expected to have
cost access at the org level.

By default, the report contains one row for each combination of budget segment and year-month. 
For example, for a budget with 10 budget segments covering 12 months, 
the report would return 120 rows (i.e., 10 segments * 12 months).

### Budgeted and Unbudgeted spend
All rows include a `budgeted` dimension with a boolean value.
It is `false` only if the row contains new dimension values from the cost data that were not described by the budget segments.

For example, if a budget defines segments for 2 specific account values, for those rows the `budgeted` dimension will be `true`.

If a 3rd account appears in the billing data, its row will be returned with the `budgeted` dimension set to `false`.

This allows you to identify the unbudgeted spend from the 3rd account. You may then wish to either:
- update the budget segments to cover the new account,
- or modify the budget's filter expression to exclude the account.

### Filtering
To narrow the report to a specific range of year-months, specify the start and end dates in the filter query parameter.

By default, the budget report returns all the budgeted and unbudgeted rows.
- Set the `budgeted` parameter to `true` to return only budgeted rows.
- Set the `budgeted` parameter to `false` to return only unbudgeted rows.

### Aggregation across budget segments
The report API can sum up results based on the requested `dimensions`.

For example, consider a budget broken down by two dimensions: Vendor and Account.

- If the `dimensions` list includes both Vendor and Account, the report will display the full budget details, with rows for potentially dozens of accounts.
- If the `dimensions` list includes only Vendor, the report will return fewer rows, providing a summary of the budget, forecast, actual spend and variance for each vendor.
- If the `dimensions` list is empty, the report will return just one row for each year-month, summarizing the total budget, forecast, actual spend and variance across all budget segments.

### Aggregation across year-months

The report API can also sum up results across year-months.

By default, it returns one row for each budget segment and year-month combination.

However, by setting the `summarized` parameter to `true`,
the report will return only one row per budget segment, 
representing its total budget, forecast, spend and variance across all the selected year-months.

parameters.description:
The filter query string parameter allows to filter reports. 

***Note:*** The value for the filter query parameter must be a URL-encoded query string.
| Filter | Required | Description | Allowed Operator | Behavior | Example |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| budgeted | No | Filter to limit returned data to just budgeted or unbudgeted rows. If `true`, only the budgeted rows will be returned. If `false`, only the unbudgeted rows will be returned.| eq | Equal - For a match, the budgeted dimension must be equal to the supplied value. | budgeted eq true |

get.description:
Lists some or all adjustment plans in the organization.

See ShowPlan to retrieve adjustment rule details.

parameters.description:
Optional filter for returning plans matching specific criteria.

Filter parameters may be combined with 'and' and 'or' logical operators.

Each parameter may compare one of the following attributes to a given value or null.

### Plan Filter Attributes
- id, the unique identifier of a plan
- name, the name of the plan
- ruleIds, the list of unique identifiers of included rules
- customerIds, the list of unique identifiers of child organizations

### Plan Filter Comparisons
- eq, attribute matches the value, e.g. planId eq 'c6671c74-513a-4127-b8df-81adfb65bf7f'
- in, attribute is one of the values, e.g. scheduled in ['before', 'after']
- co, attribute contains the value, e.g. name co 'tier'; customerIds co 1234
- lt (le), attribute is less than (or equal to) the value, e.g. endAfter le '2025-12-31'
- gt (ge), attribute is greater than (or equal to) the value, e.g. startOn ge '2024-01-01'

get.description: Retrieve an organization's access rules.

parameters.description:
Optional filter for returning access rules matching specific criteria. 

### Supported Filter Keys
| Filter     | Required | Valid Operators | Example                             | Description |
| ---        | ---      | ---             | ---                                 | ---         |
| subjectRef | no       | eq              | subjectRef eq 'ref:nam:::iam:user:123'    | Return only access rules for the user with ID 123    | 
| scopeRef   | no       | eq              | scopeRef eq 'ref:nam:::iam:org:10'        | Return only access rules for org with ID 10          |
|            |          |                 | scopeRef eq 'ref:nam:10::iam:project:100' | Return only access rules for the project with ID 100 |
| roleName   | no       | eq              | roleName eq 'org_owner'               | Return only access rules for the org_owner role      |

### Filter Notes
- Filter parameters may be combined using the 'and' logical operator
- Filter is a query parameter, and must be URL-encoded, however examples provided below will be pre-URL-encoding for clarity
- The only valid organization scope to provide is the organization in which the API call is being executed
- If the filter expression does not include any scope, the default scope is the organization

### Examples
Find access rules for a specific user

    subjectRef eq 'ref:nam:::iam:user:123'

Find access rules for a specific user in a specific project
    
    subjectRef eq 'ref:nam:::iam:user:123' and scopeRef eq 'ref:nam:10::iam:project:100'

Find access rules for a particular role
    
    roleName eq 'org_owner'

Find access rules for a specific service account, role and project

    subjectRef eq 'ref:nam:10::iam:service-account:456' and scopeRef eq 'ref:nam:10::iam:project:100' and roleName eq 'iam_admin'
parameters.name: filter

get.description:
Index returns a collection of API events which occurred within an organization, ordered from oldest
to newest.

### Pagination

If the "filter" expression includes an end timestamp (e.g. "timestamp le {date}"), this endpoint will return a
paginated list of events which occurred before the end timestamp. After all events matching the filter have been
returned, the response will not include a "nextPage" attribute. However, if the request does not include a filter
expression or the filter expression does not set an end timestamp, then an empty page indicates that all available
events have been read. In this case, responses will continue to include a "nextPage" attribute to allow the reader
to keep their place while polling for new events.

Standard Flexera [rate limits](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/page/rate-limiting) apply.

### Retention

By default, API events are retained for 3 months. Events older than 3 months will not be returned by this API. To request
a longer retention policy, please contact Flexera Customer Support.

parameters.description:
An opaque token to be provided when requesting a subsequent page after receiving a partial response. 
Partial responses will include a "nextPage" attribute in their response body, which contains the URL of the next page including the appropriate skipToken.
parameters.name: skipToken

schema.description:

parameters.description:
An optional expression for filtering the collection of API events returned.

The following filters are supported:
| Filter     | Description                          | Allowed Operator | Behavior                                                                                                        | Example                              |
| ---        | ---                                  | ---              | ---                                                                                                             | ---                                  |
| timestamp  | Filters on the API event's timestamp | le               | Less than or equal to - returns only API events with a timestamp less than or equal to the provided value       |  timestamp le '2020-10-21T10:20:50Z' |
|            |                                      | ge               | Greater than or equal to - returns only API events with a timestamp greater than or equal to the provided value |  timestamp ge '2020-10-21T10:20:50Z' |

* Operators must be lowercase

    * valid    : eq
    * invalid : EQ

* Filters can be combined using the 'and' logical operator.

    To return API events which occurred between the two timestamps:    "timestamp ge '2019-10-21T10:20:50Z' and timestamp le '2019-10-22T10:20:50Z'"

* When used as a query string, the filter parameter value must be URL-encoded:
    
        ...?filter=(timestamp%20ge%20%272019-10-21T10%3A20%3A50Z%27%20and%20timestamp%20le%20%272019-10-22T10%3A20%3A50Z%27)

* When using cURL, the same expression can be URL encoded as follows: 

        $ curl -s {$BASE_URL}/iam/v1/orgs/100/api-events \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
            -G --data-urlencode "filter=(timestamp le '2020-10-21T10:20:50Z')"

parameters.description:
Optional filter for selecting the list of customization types returned.

The following filters are supported:
| Filter | Description | Allowed Operator | Behavior | Example |
| --- | ---| --- | --- | --- |
| id | Filters on the customization type's id | co | Contains - The entire operator value must be a substring of the attribute value for a match. |  id co 'navbar' |
|    |    | eq | Equal - The attribute and operator values must be identical for a match. | id eq 'navbar-logo-url'  |
|    |    | ne | Not Equal - The attribute and operator values are not identical. | id ne 'navbar' |
| valueType | Filters on the customization type's value type | eq | Equal - The attribute and operator values must be identical for a match. | valueType eq 'URL'  |
|    |    | ne | Not Equal - The attribute and operator values are not identical. | valueType ne 'URL' |
| authenticationRequired | Filters on the customization type's authentication requirement | eq | Equal - The attribute and operator values must be identical for a match. | authenticationRequired eq 'true'  |
|    |    | ne | Not Equal - The attribute and operator values are not identical. | authenticationRequired ne 'true' |

* All operators are case-sensitive and only lowercase is allowed. 
        
        e.g: 
            valid    : eq
            invalid : EQ

* Filters can be combined using the and/or logical operator. 

        e.g: (id co 'navbar' or id eq 'navbar-logo-url')

get.description:
Index returns a collection of events which occurred within an organization, ordered from oldest to
newest.

### Pagination

If the "filter" expression includes an end timestamp (e.g. "timestamp le {date}"), this endpoint will return a
paginated list of events which occurred before the end timestamp. After all events matching the filter have been
returned, the response will not include a "nextPage" attribute. However, if the request does not include a filter
expression or the filter expression does not set an end timestamp, then an empty page indicates that all available
events have been read. In this case, responses will continue to include a "nextPage" attribute to allow the reader
to keep their place while polling for new events.

Standard Flexera [rate limits](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/page/rate-limiting) apply.

### Retention

By default, events are retained for 3 months. Events older than 3 months will not be returned by this API. To request
a longer retention policy, please contact Flexera Customer Support.

get.description: Returns the list of users who are affiliated to the org.

parameters.description:
A filter to narrow the number of users to return. Supported
                     fields in the filter are [email, firstName, lastName, lastUILogin, lastAPILogin, hasActiveRefreshToken]
The following filters are supported:
| Filter | Description | Allowed Operator | Behavior | Example |
| --- | ---| --- | --- | --- |
| email | Filters on the user's email | co | Contains - The entire operator value must be a substring of the attribute value for a match. |  email co 'company.com' |
|    |    | eq | Equal - The attribute and operator values must be identical for a match. | email eq 'jdoe@company.com'  |
|    |    | ne | Not Equal - The attribute and operator values are not identical. | email ne 'jdoe@company.com' |
| firstName | Filters on the user's firstName | co | Contains - The entire operator value must be a substring of the attribute value for a match. |  firstName co 'Jo' |
|    |    | eq | Equal - The attribute and operator values must be identical for a match. | firstName eq 'Jon'  |
|    |    | ne | Not Equal - The attribute and operator values are not identical. | firstName ne 'Jon' |
| lastName | Filters on the user's lastName | co | Contains - The entire operator value must be a substring of the attribute value for a match. |  lastName co 'Jo' |
|    |    | eq | Equal - The attribute and operator values must be identical for a match. | lastName eq 'Johnson'  |
|    |    | ne | Not Equal - The attribute and operator values are not identical. | lastName ne 'Johnson' |
| lastUILogin | Filters on the lastUILogin timestamp | gt | Greater than - The lastUILogin timestamp must be greater than the provided value for a match. |  lastUILogin gt  "2021-05-16T16:31:52.1000Z"|
|    |    | lt | Lesser than - The lastUILogin timestamp must be lesser than the provided value for a match. | lastUILogin lt  "2021-05-16T16:31:52.1000Z"  |
|    |    | ge | Greater than or equal - The lastUILogin timestamp must be greater than or equal to the provided value for a match. | lastUILogin ge  "2021-05-16T16:31:52.1000Z"  |
|    |    | le | Lesser than or equal - The lastUILogin timestamp must be lesser than or equal to the provided value for a match. | lastUILogin le  "2021-05-16T16:31:52.1000Z"  |
| lastAPILogin | Filters on the lastAPILogin timestamp | gt | Greater than - The lastAPILogin timestamp must be greater than the provided value for a match. |  lastAPILogin gt  "2021-05-16T16:31:52.1000Z"|
|    |    | lt | Lesser than - The lastAPILogin timestamp must be lesser than the provided value for a match. | lastAPILogin lt  "2021-05-16T16:31:52.1000Z"  |
|    |    | ge | Greater than or equal - The lastAPILogin timestamp must be greater than or equal to the provided value for a match. | lastAPILogin ge  "2021-05-16T16:31:52.1000Z"  |
|    |    | le | Lesser than or equal - The lastAPILogin timestamp must be lesser than or equal to the provided value for a match. | lastAPILogin le  "2021-05-16T16:31:52.1000Z"  |
| hasActiveRefreshToken | Filters on whether the user has an active refresh token | eq | Equal - The attribute and operator values must be identical for a match. | hasActiveRefreshToken eq true  |

* All operators are case-sensitive and only lowercase is allowed.

        e.g:
            valid    : eq
            invalid : EQ

* Filters can be combined using the and/or logical operator.

        e.g: (email co 'flexera.com' and lastUILogin ge '2021-05-16T16:31:52.1000Z')

* When used as a query string, the filter parameter value must be URL encoded.

        e.g: ?filter=(email%20co%20'flexera.com'%20and%20lastUILogin%20ge%20'2021-05-16T16:31:52.1000Z')

    When using cURL, the same expression can be URL encoded as follows:

        $ curl -s {$BASE_URL}/iam/v1/orgs/{$ORG_ID}/users \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
            -G --data-urlencode "filter=(email co 'flexera.com' and lastUILogin ge '2021-05-16T16:31:52.1000Z')"

patch.description:
Updates the first name and/or last name of a user affiliated to an org.

**Required privilege**: iam:org_user:update (org_owner or equivalent).

**Multi-org security**: The caller must have admin access in *every* org the target user
belongs to. If the user is affiliated with orgs A, B, and C, the caller needs access
in all three — not just the org specified in the request. This prevents an admin in one
org from modifying a shared user's name without consent from admins in other orgs.

**Sync guard**: A successful update sets an internal `updated_by` marker
(`admin:{callerID}`) on the user record. The User Management Service uses this
marker to reject subsequent AD/SAML sync writes that would overwrite the manually-set
name. The marker is cleared when the IdP profile master sync next runs with a value
that matches the current name.

**isNameManagedByIDP**: The response includes this flag. When `true`, the org's SAML
IDP has profile-master enabled, meaning the name edit may be overridden on the user's
next SSO login if the AD/SAML attribute mapping still points to a different value.

patch.description:
Updates the first name and/or last name of the currently authenticated user.
Only fields provided in the request body are updated — omitting a field leaves it unchanged.

**Sync guard**: A successful update sets an internal `updated_by` marker
(`user:{callerID}`) on the user record in UMS. The User Management Service uses this
marker to reject subsequent AD/SAML sync writes that would overwrite the manually-set
name. This protects users whose IdP has incorrect or stale attribute mappings from having
their name reverted every time they log in via SSO.

**No org context required**: The update applies globally to the user record, regardless
of which org they are editing from. The change is reflected in all org contexts.

**Response**: Returns 200 OK with the updated profile on success.

get.description: Index a managed service provider's list of customer tenants.

parameters.description:
Optional filter for filtering list of customers returned. 

The following filters are supported:
| Filter | Description | Allowed Operator | Behavior | Example |
| --- | ---| --- | --- | --- |
| name | Filters on the organization name | co | Contains - The entire operator value must be a substring of the attribute value for a match. |  name co 'SAP' |
|    |    | eq | Equal - The attribute and operator values must be identical for a match. | name eq 'HP'  |
|    |    | ne | Not Equal - The attribute and operator values are not identical. | name ne 'SAP' |

* All operators are case-sensitive and only lowercase is allowed. 
        
        e.g: 
            valid    : eq
            invalid : EQ

* Filters can be combined using the and/or logical operator. 

        e.g: (name co 'SAP' or name eq 'HP')
    
* When used as a query string, the filter parameter value must be URL encoded.         
    
        e.g: ?filter=(name%20co%20'SAP'%20or%20name%20eq%20'HP')

    When using cURL, the same expression can be URL encoded as follows: 

        $ curl -s {$BASE_URL}/msp/v1/orgs/{$ORG_ID}/customers \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
            -G --data-urlencode "filter=(name co 'SAP' or name eq 'HP')"

parameters.description:
Optional filter for filtering list of customers returned. 

The following filters are supported:
| Filter | Description | Allowed Operator | Behavior | Example |
| --- | ---| --- | --- | --- |
| name | Filters on the organization name | co | Contains - The entire operator value must be a substring of the attribute value for a match. |  name co 'SAP' |
|    |    | eq | Equal - The attribute and operator values must be identical for a match. | name eq 'HP'  |
|    |    | ne | Not Equal - The attribute and operator values are not identical. | name ne 'SAP' |

* All operators are case-sensitive and only lowercase is allowed. 
        
        e.g: 
            valid    : eq
            invalid : EQ

* Filters can be combined using the and/or logical operator. 

        e.g: (name co 'SAP' or name eq 'HP')
    
* When used as a query string, the filter parameter value must be URL encoded.         
    
        e.g: ?filter=(name%20co%20'SAP'%20or%20name%20eq%20'HP')

    When using cURL, the same expression can be URL encoded as follows: 

        $ curl -s {$BASE_URL}/msp/v2/orgs/{$ORG_ID}/customers \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
            -G --data-urlencode "filter=(name co 'SAP' or name eq 'HP')"

This endpoint creates a new customer organization under the specified MSP parent organization. 
The newly created organization is immediately available and functional. Owners specified in the request

* Enforces hierarchy width limits - prevents creation if parent has reached max_width children
* Returns specific error codes for constraint violations to help diagnose issues

Note: Capabilities granted to the customer organization must be a subset of the capabilities 
available to the MSP parent organization.

post.description:
BulkCreate provisions multiple customer tenants for a managed service provider in a single request. 
This operation is limited to 100 customers in a single request.
Individual customer creation attempts can succeed or fail independently. The response includes detailed 
status information for each customer creation attempt, along with summary statistics.

Use the optional 'status' query parameter to filter which results are included in the response:
- Without filter: returns all results (both successful and failed)
- status=success: returns only successfully created customers
- status=failed: returns only failed customer creation attempts

V2 API enhancements over v1:
* Validates MSP capability hierarchy constraints (max_depth, max_width) for each customer during creation
* Enforces hierarchy depth limits - prevents creating MSP children if parent's max_depth is 0
* Enforces hierarchy width limits - prevents creation if parent has reached max_width children
* Returns specific error codes for constraint violations in individual results

Note: Capabilities granted to each customer organization must be a subset of the capabilities 
available to the MSP parent organization.

get.description:
Index returns a list of published templates which can be filtered by the catalogSource parameter. 
The default setting only includes templates made available to all MSP child orgs.
Using different catalogSource value enables users to preview what templates will be available to their child orgs with other "policy-catalog-reference-org" settings.
This setting can be changed at the [Customization Value](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/api/policy/v1#/Customization%20Value) endpoint.

parameters.description:
Optional filter to retrieve published templates based on specific criteria.
### Supported Filter Keys
| Filter                    | Type   | Example                                   | Description                                                                           |
| ------------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------    | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| name                      | string | name in ['policy123', 'policy124']        | Returns published templates named either 'policy123' or 'policy124'                   |
| shortDescription          | string | shortDescription co 'disks'               | Returns published templates with a shortDescription containing 'disks'                |
| longDescription           | string | longDescription co 'cloud'                | Returns published templates with a longDescription containing 'cloud'                 |
| docLink                   | string | docLink co 'README'                       | Returns published templates with a docLink containing 'README'                        |
| category                  | string | category in ['compliance', 'cost']        | Returns published templates with 'compliance' or 'cost' as category                   |
| createdBy.email           | string | createdBy.email eq 'foouser@email.com'    | Returns published templates created by user with email equal to 'foouser@email.com'   |
| createdAt                 | time   | createdAt gt '2022-05-20T00:00:00Z'       | Returns published templates created after 2022-05-20                                  |
| updatedAt                 | time   | updatedAt lt '2020-01-01T00:00:00Z'       | Returns published templates updated before 2020-01-01                                 |
| builtIn                   | bool   | builtIn eq false                          | Returns published templates that are not built-in                                     |
| hidden                    | bool   | hidden eq true                            | Returns published templates that are hidden                                           |

### Supported Operators
- **in** - Checks if the field contains a specified value within a list.
- **eq** - Checks if the field's value is equal to the specified value.
- **ne** - Checks if the field's value is not equal to the specified value.
- **co** - Checks if the field contains the specified substring.
- **and, or** - Logical operators used to combine multiple conditions.
- **not** - Logical operator negates the condition that follows it.
- **lt, gt, le, ge** - Relational operators used to compare the field's value against a specified value. They check for less than, greater than, less than or equal to, and greater than or equal to conditions, respectively.

### Notes
- The filter is a query parameter. While it needs to be URL-encoded, examples here are provided pre-URL-encoding for clarity.

### Examples
| Example                                                                    | Description                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| name co 'Azure' and category eq 'operational'                              | Find published templates whose name contain 'Azure' and are categorized as 'operational'          |
| name co 'instances' and category in ['compliance', 'cost']                 | Find published templates whose name contain 'instances' and 'compliance' or 'cost' as category    |
| shortDescription co 'deprecated' and category eq 'compliance'              | Find published templates whose shortDescription contain 'deprecated' and 'compliance' as category |
| createdAt gt '2022-05-20T00:00:00Z' or updatedAt gt '2022-05-20T00:00:00Z' | Find published templates created or updated after 2022-05-20                                      |
| builtIn eq true and tenancy eq 'single'                                    | Find published templates that are built-in whose tenancy is set to true                           |

parameters.description:
Optional filter to retrieve incident aggregates based on specific criteria.
### Supported Filter Keys
| Filter     | Type   | Example                              | Description                                                      |
| ---------- | ------ | ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| severity   | string | severity in ['high', 'critical']     | Returns incident aggregates whose severity is high or critical.  |
| createdAt  | time   | createdAt gt '2023-10-10T00:00:00Z'  | Returns incident aggregates created after 2023-10-10.            |
| updatedAt  | time   | updatedAt lt '2024-01-09T00:00:00Z'  | Returns incident aggregates updated before 2024-01-09.           |
| category   | string | category eq 'cost'                   | Returns incident aggregates whose category is cost.              |
| dryRun     | bool   | dryRun eq false                      | Returns incident aggregates whose dryRun is set to false.        |

### Supported Operators
- **in** - Checks if the field contains a specified value within a list.
- **eq** - Checks if the field's value is equal to the specified value.
- **ne** - Checks if the field's value is not equal to the specified value.
- **co** - Checks if the field contains the specified substring.
- **and, or** - Logical operators used to combine multiple conditions.
- **not** - Logical operator negates the condition that follows it.
- **lt, gt, le, ge** - Relational operators used to compare the field's value against a specified value. They check for less than, greater than, less than or equal to, and greater than or equal to conditions, respectively.

### Notes
- The filter is a query parameter. While it needs to be URL-encoded, examples here are provided pre-URL-encoding for clarity.

### Examples
| Example                                                  | Description                                                                               |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| category eq 'Cost' and dryRun eq true                    | Find incident aggregates whose category is Cost and dryRun is set to true.                |
| dryRun eq false and createdAt gt '2023-10-10T00:00:00Z'  | Find incident aggregates whose dryRun is set to false and were created after 2023-10-10.  |
| severity eq 'high' or category eq 'security'             | Find incident aggregates whose severity is high or category is security.                  |

parameters.description:
Optional filter to retrieve policy aggregates based on specific criteria.

### Supported Filter Keys
| Filter                 | Type   | Example                             | Description                                                     |
| ---------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------| --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| name                   | string | name in ['policy123', 'policy124']  | Returns policy aggregates named either policy123 or policy124   |
| projectIds             | number | projectIds in [10017, 10134]        | Returns policy aggregates from either project 10017 or 10134    |
| status                 | string | status co 'active'                  | Returns policy aggregates with a status containing 'active'     |
| createdBy.email        | number | createdBy.email eq 'test@gmail.com' | Returns policy aggregates created by user with specified email  |
| createdAt              | time   | createdAt gt '2022-05-20T00:00:00Z' | Returns policy aggregates created after the start of the date   |
| updatedAt              | time   | updatedAt lt '2022-05-20T00:00:00Z' | Returns policy aggregates updated before 2022-05-20             |
| schedule               | string | schedule eq 'FREQ=DAILY'            | Returns policy aggregates with a specified schedule             |
| publishedTemplate.name | string | publishedTemplate.name co 'AWS'     | Returns policy aggregates with a template name containing 'AWS' |
| category               | string | category eq 'security'              | Returns policy aggregates in the 'security' category            |
| dryRun                 | bool   | dryRun eq true                      | Returns policy aggregates with dryRun set to true               |

### Supported Operators

- **in** - Checks if the field contains a specified value within a list.
- **eq** - Checks if the field's value is equal to the specified value.
- **ne** - Checks if the field's value is not equal to the specified value.
- **co** - Checks if the field contains the specified substring.
- **and, or** - Logical operators used to combine multiple conditions.
- **not** - Logical operator negates the condition that follows it.
- **lt, gt, le, ge** - Relational operators used to compare the field's value against a specified value. They check for less than, greater than, less than or equal to, and greater than or equal to conditions, respectively.

### Notes
- The filter is a query parameter. While it needs to be URL-encoded, examples here are provided pre-URL-encoding for clarity.

### Examples
| Example                                                            | Description                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| name co 'Azure'                                                    | Find policies with a name containing the word 'Azure'                       |
| name in ['policy123', 'policy124'] and project in [10017, 10134] | Retrieve policies with any of the specified names from specific projects |

Optional filter to retrieve policy managers based on specific criteria.

### Supported Filter Keys
| Filter                 | Type   | Example                              | Description                                                     |
| ---------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| name                   | string | name in ['policy123', 'policy124']   | Returns policy managers named either policy123 or policy124     |
| status                 | string | status co 'active'                   | Returns policy managers with a status containing 'active'       |
| createdBy.email        | string | createdBy.email eq 'test@gmail.com'  | Returns policy managers created by user with specified email    |
| createdAt              | time   | createdAt gt '2022-05-20T00:00:00Z'  | Returns policy managers created after the start of the date     |
| updatedAt              | time   | updatedAt lt '2022-05-20T00:00:00Z'  | Returns policy managers updated before 2022-05-20               |
| schedule               | string | schedule eq 'daily'                  | Returns policy managers with a specified schedule               |
| publishedTemplate.name | string | publishedTemplate.name co 'AWS'      | Returns policy managers with a template name containing 'AWS'   |
| dryRun                 | bool   | dryRun eq true                       | Returns policy managers with dryRun set to true                 |

### Supported Operators

- **in** - Checks if the field contains a specified value within a list.
- **eq** - Checks if the field's value is equal to the specified value.
- **ne** - Checks if the field's value is not equal to the specified value.
- **co** - Checks if the field contains the specified substring.
- **has** - Checks if an array field contains the specified value.
- **and, or** - Logical operators used to combine multiple conditions.
- **not** - Logical operator negates the condition that follows it.
- **lt, gt, le, ge** - Relational operators used to compare the field's value against a specified value. They check for less than, greater than, less than or equal to, and greater than or equal to conditions, respectively.

### Notes
- The filter is a query parameter. While it needs to be URL-encoded, examples here are provided pre-URL-encoding for clarity.

parameters.description:
Optional filter for returning applied policies matching specific criteria.
### Supported Filter Keys
| Filter                  | Type   | Example                                               | Description                                                                                          |
| ---------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| name                    | string | name in ['policy123', 'policy124']                    | Returns applied policies with named either policy123 or policy124                                      |
| metaParentPolicyId     | string | metaParentPolicyId eq '5b06ead5e0dacc007058c784'   | Returns applied policies with metaParentPolicyId equal to '5b06ead5e0dacc007058c784'                 |
| recommendationSetId     | string | recommendationSetId eq '5b06ead5e0dacc007058c784'  | Returns applied policies with recommendationSetId equal to'5b06ead5e0dacc007058c784'                 |
| status                  | string | status co 'active'                                   | Returns applied policies with 'status' containing 'active' word                                      |
| createdBy.email          | string | createdBy.email eq 'foouser@email.com'             | Returns applied policies created by user with email equals to 'foouser@email.com'                    |
| createdAt              | time   | createdAt gt '2022-05-20T00:00:00Z'                  | Returns applied policies created after 2022-05-20                                                    |
| updatedAt              | time   | updatedAt lt '2020-01-01T00:00:00Z'                  | Returns applied policies updated before 2020-01-01                                                    |
| schedule               | string | schedule eq 'FREQ=MONTHLY'                          | Returns applied policies with a specific schedule                                                      |
| policyTemplate.name       | string | policyTemplate.name co 'AWS'                       | Returns applied policies with policy template name containing 'AWS' word                               |
| publishedTemplate.name | string | publishedTemplate.name eq 'Demo template'          | Returns applied policies with published template name equals to 'Demo template'                       |
| category                    | string | category eq 'security'                                | Returns applied policies with 'security' as category                                                  |
| dryRun                 | bool   | dryRun eq true                                       | Returns applied policies with dryRun (Test mode) as true                                            |
| templateName            | string | templateName in ['temp1', 'pubTemp1']                 | Returns applied policies with policy/published template name either temp1 or pubTemp1                |
| policyTemplate.id       | string | policyTemplate.id eq '5b06ead5e0baca007058c784'    | Returns applied policies with policy template id equal to '5b06ead5e0baca007058c784'                 |
| publishedTemplate.id     | string | publishedTemplate.id eq '65b1a38500aea214ee7437ed' | Returns applied policies with published template id equal to '65b1a38500aea214ee7437ed'            |

### Supported Operators
- **in** - Checks if the field contains a specified value within a list.
- **eq** - Checks if the field's value is equal to the specified value.
- **ne** - Checks if the field's value is not equal to the specified value.
- **co** - Checks if the field contains the specified substring.
- **and, or** - Logical operators used to combine multiple conditions.
- **not** - Logical operator negates the condition that follows it.
- **lt, gt, le, ge** - Relational operators used to compare the field's value against a specified value. They check for less than, greater than, less than or equal to, and greater than or equal to conditions, respectively.

### Notes
- The filter is a query parameter. While it needs to be URL-encoded, examples here are provided pre-URL-encoding for clarity.

### Examples
| Example                                                             | Description                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| name eq 'policy123'                                                 | Find applied policies for a specific name                                      |
| name eq 'policy123' or name eq 'policy456'                         | Find applied policies named 'policy123' or named 'policy456'                     |
| metaParentPolicyId eq '5b06ead5e0dacc007058c784'                     | Find applied policies for a particular metaParentPolicyId                        |
| name co 'Azure'                                                     | Find applied policies with a name containing the word 'Azure'                   |
| status eq 'active'                                                 | Find applied policies with 'active' status                                       |
| createdAt gt '2022-05-20T00:00:00Z' or schedule eq 'FREQ=MONTHLY' | Find applied policies created after 2022-05-20 or with a specific schedule   |
| dryRun eq true and category eq 'security'                         | Find applied policies where dryRun is set to true and category is 'security' |

get.description: Retrieve summarized data around discovered application usage.

parameters.description:
The filter to query discovered app usage . Supported fields in the filter are [source.managedAppId, name, category, snapshotAt]
|   Attribute         | Description                                                            | Allowed Operators      |        Example                           |
|---------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| source.managedAppId | Filter summarized discovered app usage by Source Managed AppID        | eq                     | source.managedAppId eq '378432'         |
| name                  | Filter summarized discovered app usage by Name                              | eq, in, nin, co, ne  | name eq 'Salesforce'                       |
| category              | Filter summarized discovered app usage by Category                          | eq, in, nin, co, ne  | category eq 'News'                       |
| snapshotAt          | Filter summarized discovered app usage by snapshot date                  | ge, le                 | snapshotAt ge '2017-05-01T00:00:00.000Z'|
* All filter values and operators are not case sensitive.

        e.g:
            valid : eq
            valid : EQ
* Filters can be combined using the 'and/or' logical operator.
        e.g: (source.managedAppId eq '378432' or name eq 'Salesforce')

post.description:
The query endpoint takes in a metric query request, pulls the relevant raw data from the 
            metrics service and, marshals the result into a query result.

## Stored Queries
        
Here is a description of each default stored query available.
| queryName                        | Description                                                                                                                            |
|---------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| departmentSpend                  | The amount spent per department within the scope of the managed application. This query requires organizational data to be available.  |
| applicationUsage                 | The number of active/inactive/never active app users within the activity threshold.                                                    |
| applicationUsageOverTime         | The number of active/inactive/never active app users over a given time period.                                                         |
| daysSinceActiveRange             | The number of active/inactive/never application users within the given time range.                                                     |
| licenseUsage                     | The number of active/inactive/never application users per managed application per license.                                             |
| licenseUsageOverTime             | The number of active/inactive/never application users per managed application per license over a given time period .                   |
| totalNumberOfUsers             | The number of total app users within the activity threshold.                                                                           |
| totalNumberOfUsersOverTime        | The number of total app users over a given time period.                                                                                |
| orgInfo                          | The estimated amount spent, number of active managed apps, licenses and total inactive, never active users for entire org are returned.|
| orgGroupSpend                    | The amount spent per department for each department in the org, sorted by amount desc                                                  |
| orgApplicationUsage              | The number of active/inactive/never active app users within the activity threshold for all apps in the org, sorted by total users desc.|

## Dimensions
Dimensions that the query can be split upon.
| Dimensions     | Description                                                                                                                                                             |
|----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| resourceType   | If there is more than one resourceType can be a value such as appUser. If there are more resourceTypes available, they show up in the resourceType dimension construct. |
| group          | The groups as defined by the organizational data. For example, if department is available, the data will be split by department.                                        |
| resourceStatus | If the resource, such as AppUser has a status of active, never active, or inactive, the result will be split along those lines.                                            |

## Granularity
| Granularity  | Description                                                                  |
|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| day          | Each data point represents 24 hours in UTC.                                  |
| month        | Each data point represents an entire calendar month of data.                 |
| firstOfMonth | Each data point represents the first of the month of each month of the year. |

## Metrics
| Granularity  | Description                                                                  |
|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| day          | Each data point represents 24 hours in UTC.                                  |
| month        | Each data point represents an entire calendar month of data.                 |
| firstOfMonth | Each data point represents the first of the month of each month of the year. |

## Filter
| Filter       | Description                                                       |
|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| managedAppId | The managed application id                                        |
| date         | A date in the format YYYY-MM-DD                                   |
| sku          | This value allows the filtering down to a particular license sku. |

## Currency 

The currency (default is USD) can be set globally in Administration -> SaaS Settings -> General within app.flexera.com.

parameters.description:
The date filter to query the usage groups. Supported fields in the filter are [managedAppId, sourceId, appUser, usageGroup]
|   Attribute   | Description                                                 | Allowed Operators |        Example             |
|---------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------------------------|
| managedAppId  | Filter usage consumption by their Managed AppID             | eq                | managedAppId eq '378432'   |
| sourceId      | Filter usage consumption by their sourceId                  | eq                | sourceId eq     '986435'   |
| appUser       | Filter usage consumption by their appUser                   | eq                | appUser eq      '119723'   |
| usageGroup    | Filter usage consumption by their usageGroup                | eq                | usageGroup eq 'Contacts'   |
* All filter values and operators are not case sensitive.

        e.g:
            valid : eq
            valid : EQ
* Filters can be combined using the 'and/or' logical operator.
        e.g: (managedAppId eq '378432' or sourceId eq '986435')

* When used as a query string, the filter parameter value must be URL-encoded.

    e.g: ?filter=(managedAppId%20eq%20'378432'%20or%20sourceId%20eq%20'986435')
    When using cURL, the same expression can be URL encoded as follows:

        $ curl -s {$BASE_URL}/ent/v1/orgs/{$ORG_ID}/contracts \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
            -G --data-urlencode "filter=(managedAppId eq '378432' and 20sourceId eq '986435')"

get.description:
Index returns a list of groups for an org.

This API returns the members attribute as an empty array in index responses. To retrieve members, call GET /scim/v2/orgs/{orgId}/Groups/{id}.

parameters.description:
A filter to narrow the number of groups to return. Supported
                     fields in the filter are [id, displayName]
The following filters are supported:
| Filter | Description | Allowed Operator | Behavior | Example |
| --- | ---| --- | --- | --- |
| id | Filters on the group's ID | eq | Equal - The attribute and operator values must be identical for a match. |  id eq '123' |
| displayName | Filters on the group's displayName | eq | Equal - The attribute and operator values must be identical for a match. |  displayName eq 'Admins' |

* All operators are case-insensitive according to RFC 7644.

        e.g:
            valid  : eq
            valid  : EQ

* When used as a query string, the filter parameter value must be URL encoded.

        e.g: ?filter=(id%20eq%20'586859'%20)

    When using cURL, the same expression can be URL encoded as follows:

        $ curl -s {$BASE_URL}/scim/v2/orgs/{$ORG_ID}/Groups \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
            -G --data-urlencode "filter=(id eq '586859')"

parameters.description:
A filter to narrow the number of users to return. Supported
                     fields in the filter are [id, UserName]
The following filters are supported:
| Filter | Description | Allowed Operator | Behavior | Example |
| --- | ---| --- | --- | --- |
| id | Filters on the user's ID | eq | Equal - The attribute and operator values must be identical for a match. |  id eq '123' |
| UserName | Filters on the user's UserName | eq | Equal - The attribute and operator values must be identical for a match. |  UserName eq 'Jon' |

* All operators are case-insensitive according to RFC 7644.

        e.g:
            valid  : eq
            valid  : EQ

* When used as a query string, the filter parameter value must be URL encoded.

        e.g: ?filter=(id%20eq%20'586859'%20)

    When using cURL, the same expression can be URL encoded as follows:

        $ curl -s {$BASE_URL}/scim/v2/orgs/{$ORG_ID}/users \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
            -G --data-urlencode "filter=(id eq '586859')"

parameters.description:
Advanced filter expression for querying connectors.

### Supported Fields & Operators

| Field           | Operators | Description                               |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------------------------------------|
| connectorName   | eq, co    | Exact or contains match on connector name |
| accountId       | eq, co    | Exact / contains match on account ID      |
| provider        | in        | Allowed values based on caller access     |
| createdAt       | ge, le    | Timestamp range filtering                 |
| masterAccountId | eq, co    | Match against master account ID           |
| enrollmentStatus| in        | allowed: ONBOARDED, OFFBOARDED, FAILED, IN-PROGRESS|
| onboardingType  | in        | Filter by type: 'Auto Discovery', 'Individual', 'Linked' |
| billingAccountId| eq, co    | Exact / contains match on billing acct ID |
| products        | in        | Allowed values: 'di', 'bpc', 'cco', 'oe', 'ai'  |

### Formatting Rules

- Operators must be lowercase
- Values must be wrapped in single quotes: `'value'`
- Multiple conditions must be joined using `and`
- Timestamp must use strict ISO format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffZ`

### Examples

- `connectorName co 'aws'`
- `accountId eq '123456789012'`
- `accountId co '1234'`
- `masterAccountId eq '987654321000'`
- `masterAccountId co '9876'`
- `enrollmentStatus in ['ONBOARDED','OFFBOARDED','FAILED']`
- `provider in ['aws','azure']`
- `createdAt ge '2025-11-01T00:00:00.00Z' and createdAt le '2025-11-30T23:59:00.59Z'`
- `enrollmentStatus in ['error'] and connectorName co 'finops'`
- `onboardingType in ['Auto Discovery','Individual']`
- `billingAccountId eq '123456789012'`
- `billingAccountId co '1234'`
- `products in ['di','bpc']`
- `products in ['oe']`
- `products in ['ai']`
parameters.name: filter

get.description:
Index returns a list of inventory exports to which an org has access.
        Retrieves file list by filter params

parameters.description:
Optional filter for returning requests matching specific criteria.

The following filters are supported:
| Filter | Description | Allowed Operator | Behavior | Example |
| --- | ---| --- | --- | --- |
| id   | Filters on the export id | eq | Equal - The attribute and operator values must be identical for a match  | id eq '12345'  |
| name | Filters on the export name | co | Contains - The entire operator value must be a substring of the attribute value for a match. |  name co 'hardware' |
|      |  | eq | Equal - The attribute and operator values must be identical for a match. | name eq 'hardware_technopedia'  |
| type | Filters on the type | eq | Equal - The attribute and operator values must be identical for a match. | type eq 'Delta'  |
| createdAt | Filters on the createdAt | eq | Equal - The attribute and operator values must be identical for a match. | createdAt eq '2022-02-22'  |
| size  | Filters on the export Size | gt | Greater than - The attribute must be greater than than operator values for a match. | size gt '150'  |
|      |  | lt | Less than - The attribute must be less than than operator values for a match. | size gt '150'  |

* All operators are case-sensitive and only lowercase is allowed. 
        
        e.g: 
            valid    : eq
            invalid : EQ
* Filters can be combined using the and/or logical operator. 
        e.g: (name co 'hardware' or name eq 'software_technopedia')
    
* When used as a query string, the filter parameter value must be URL encoded.         
    
        e.g: ?filter=(name%20co%20'hardware'%20or%20name%20eq%20'software_technopedia')
    When using cURL, the same expression can be URL encoded as follows: 
        $ curl -s {$BASE_URL}/vis/v2/orgs/{$ORG_ID}/exports \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
            -G --data-urlencode "filter=(name co 'hardware' or name eq 'software_technopedia')"

AWS STS supports signing requests using

Note that other Flexera services may have additional documentation for use of AWS STS Credentials.
tags.name: AWS STS Credential

tags.description:
Access policies provide a higher-level abstraction for managing role-based access control in Flexera One.
An access policy encapsulates multiple IAM roles and their associated granular scoped permissions, allowing administrators 
to define and apply consistent access patterns across user groups.

### Key Components
- **IAM Roles**: Collections of permissions that define what actions can be performed
- **Granular Scoped Permissions**: Fine-grained permissions that specify access to specific resources or resource types
- **Granular Scopes**: Define the context or boundaries within which permissions apply

### Use Cases
Access policies are particularly useful for:
- Standardizing access patterns across similar user roles
- Simplifying bulk permission assignments 
- Managing complex permission sets as cohesive units
- Ensuring consistent security policies across organizations

Access policies support flexible input formats, allowing nested resources to be specified either by ID reference 
(for existing resources) or by providing full creation parameters (for new resources) within a single atomic operation.
tags.name: Access Policy

tags.description:
An access rule grants permission to a subject, and has three components: a subject, role and scope. A subject may be granted any number of roles within a scope, and their level of permission is the union of all roles they are granted. 
### Subject
A subject is an entity to which permission is granted. 
The subject is referred to by its [ref](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/page/resource-references).
| Subject         | Ref Format               | Detail |
| ---             | ---                      | ---    |
| user            | ref:{zone}:::iam:user:{ID}                   | A user is an individual with access to Flexera One, who may have access to one or more organizations. |
| service account | ref:{zone}:{orgID}::iam:service-account:{ID} | A service account is an account used by an application to interact with Flexera One APIs. It can access only the organization it exists within. |
| group           | ref:{zone}:{orgID}::iam:group:{ID}           | A group is a collection of users. Roles granted to the group apply to all users within the group. |

### Scope
A scope is a context within which resources may exist and roles may be granted. 
A Flexera One organization is itself a scope. 
Organizations may also have one or more projects, each of which is a distinct scope.
The scope is referred to by its [ref](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/page/resource-references).
| Scope      | Ref Format                       | Detail |
| ---        | ---                              | ---    |
| org        | ref:{zone}:::iam:org:{ID}            | A role granted within the organization scope grants permission within the organization, and each of the organization's projects. | 
| project    | ref:{zone}:{orgID}::iam:project:{ID} | A role granted within a project grants permission only within that project. |

### Role
A role is a specific level of permission. Refer to the IAM Roles API or [Flexera One Roles](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Administration/flexeraroles.htm) to understand details of each role.
tags.name: Access Rule

tags.description:
**In Preview: not currently supported in production.**
    
An action status is the status of an action after it is executed by an [escalation](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Automation/Escalations.htm) or by a [resolution](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Automation/Resolutions.htm) raised by an [incident](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Automation/AboutPolicies.htm#aboutpolicies_2371672742_1084494) of an [applied policy template](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/api/policy/v1#/Applied%20Policy).

Actions can be sending emails, requesting manual approvals, or running cloud workflows. The possible statuses for actions are:

- Queued: The initial status of an action.
- Aborted: When the incident of the action was deleted.
- Pending: When awaiting the user's approval.
- Running: When the action is in progress.
- Completed: When all the tasks for an action are completed.
- Failed: When the action had an error.
- Denied: When the user denies the action.

**Escalations** are sequences of actions that are triggered when a policy validation fails, indicating a compliance or configuration issue.

**Resolutions** are sequences of actions that are executed when a previously failed policy condition is corrected, indicating that compliance has been restored.
tags.name: Action Status
