An Archived Incident is a partial copy of an eligible inactive [incident](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Automation/AboutPolicies.htm#aboutpolicies_2371672742_1084494) which has been deleted during the archiving process.

Inactive incidents are incidents which either have had their associated applied policy terminated or incidents which have been resolved. Inactive incidents become eligible to be archived after 30 days of entering that terminated or resolved state. Resolved incidents which currently have one or more resolutions running on them will not be archived until all resolutions have finished running.

During the archiving process all incident fields except the data and detail will be saved to the archived incident and then the incident will be deleted. The archived incident will remain accessible for one year before it is permanently deleted as well.
tags.name: Archived Incident

AWS bill connect provides a resource for registering and maintaining AWS bill connections.
   This offer two ways of connecting AWS bills, using IAM Role (cross-account role) or IAM user.
   The preferred method for connecting to AWS, cross-account roles allow you to grant Flexera access to your account in a defined and constrained way.
   IAM users provide broad access to AWS services. Where possible, we recommend using cross-account roles.

See
[FinOps Bill Connect Configs AWS](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Administration/BillConnectConfigsAWS.htm)
for more details.
tags.name: Bill Connect - AWS

tags.description:
Azure CSP (CSP Partner Center) Bill Connect provides a resource for registering and maintaining Azure CSP Bill Connections at the Billing Account scope.
    This bill connect uses Azure's Service Principals with a Client Secret under the hood for authentication with Microsoft's APIs.
    Billing account for the CSP contains one or more billing profiles that let you manage your invoices and payment methods. 
    Each billing profile contains one or more invoice sections that let you organize costs on the billing profile's invoice.
tags.name: Bill Connect - Azure CSP

tags.description:

    This bill connect supports scoped data ingestion at three billing levels: Billing Account (default), Billing Profile, and Invoice Section.
    This bill connect uses Azure's Service Principals with a Client Secret under the hood for authentication with Microsoft's APIs.
    Billing account for the Microsoft Customer Agreement contains one or more billing profiles that let you manage your invoices and payment methods. 
    Each billing profile contains one or more invoice sections that let you organize costs on the billing profile's invoice.
tags.name: Bill Connect - Azure MCA

The Billing APIs allow you to define and edit rules that alter how your cloud bills are interpreted. Among other use cases, this supports reselling cloud services to external customers or charging back services to internal teams.

This API offers ways to manage adjustment rules, which define operations that reinterpret cloud bills. Rules are organized into four main collections:

- Adjustment Pre-Plan Rules: rules that typically apply to a single child organization.

Depending on your license, you may have access to Enterprise Adjustment Rules or to the other three collections.

tags.description:
See: [https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Optima/cloudbudgets.htm](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Optima/cloudbudgets.htm)

The Budget API provides functionality for both Budgeting and Forecasting, enabling users to analyze planned budgets and forecasts against actual spend.

The API allows you to create, read, update, and delete budgets, as well as generate budget reports to compare your planned budget and forecast with actual spend. Budgets are defined using a combination of dimensions, year-months, and segments to provide a flexible and detailed breakdown of your costs.

A budget is defined with the following properties:

- `name`: A descriptive name to uniquely identify the budget.
- `metric`: The cost metric used for the budget. Supported values include v1 metrics (`cost_amortized_unblended_adj`, `cost_nonamortized_unblended_adj`) and v2 FOCUS metrics (`BilledCost`, `EffectiveCost`, `ModifiedBilledCost`, `ModifiedEffectiveCost`).
- `dimensions`: An array of dimensions used for budget breakdown, such as `ProviderName`, or `rbd_team`.
- `yearMonths`: An array of year-month strings like `"2023-01"`, defining the time period covered by the budget.
- `segments`: An array of budget segments, like rows in a spreadsheet. Each segment describes a combination of dimension values and the corresponding budget amount and forecast amount for each year-month.
- `filter`: An optional filter expression to narrow down the scope of the budget based on specific dimension values. This is useful later when generating a budget report, as it allows you to exclude certain line items from the report rather than marking them as "unbudgeted". For example, you might define the budget filter to only include AWS costs, and exclude all Tax line items from the budget.

Here's an example budget for "2023 Q1" listing the expected costs for each ProviderName, for the first three months of the year:
```json
{
  "name": "2023 Q1",
  "metric": "BilledCost",
  "dimensions": ["ProviderName"],
  "yearMonths": ["2023-01", "2023-02", "2023-03"],
  "segments": [
    {"dimensionValues": ["AWS"], "budgetAmounts": [100, 110, 120], "forecastAmounts":  [110, 100, 130]},
    {"dimensionValues": ["GCP"], "budgetAmounts": [200, 230, 240], "forecastAmounts":  [210, 200, 230]}
  ]
}
```

For full details on the budget properties, please refer to the Budget CRUD actions below.

## Decentralized Access
The Budget API allows decentralized access to budget reports by controlling access at the segment level. It does this by leveraging the existing billing center privileges.

The "Billing Center Level" dimensions (ex: "Billing Center Level 1") can be used in budgets to enable this behaviour, since they identify which billing center the costs are assigned to.

Let's consider an organization with the following billing center hierarchy: 
- Oaktree
  - Marketing
  - Engineering
  - Sales
    - Support
- Redwood
  - R & D
  - Marketing

The Billing Center Level dimensions would be populated with these combinations of values, representing the path that the costs were assigned to.

| Billing Center Level 1 | Billing Center Level 2 | Billing Center Level 3 |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Oaktree                | Marketing              |                        |
| Oaktree                | Engineering            |                        |
| Oaktree                | Sales                  | Support                |
| Redwood                | R & D                  |                        |
| Redwood                | Marketing              |                        |

Note: the values would actually be billing center IDs, but here we'll use the billing center names for legibility.

A budget created with a Billing Center Level dimension will control access to reports at the segment level.

Here, we'll modify the above "2023 Q1" budget to be further broken down by the "Billing Center Level 1" dimension:
```json
{
  "name": "2023 Q1",
  "metric": "EffectiveCost",
  "dimensions": ["bc_level_1", "ProviderName"],
  "yearMonths": ["2023-01", "2023-02", "2023-03"],
  "segments": [
    {"dimensionValues": ["Oaktree", "AWS"], "budgetAmounts": [50,   55,  60]},
    {"dimensionValues": ["Oaktree", "GCP"], "budgetAmounts": [100, 115, 120]},
    {"dimensionValues": ["Redwood", "AWS"], "budgetAmounts": [55,   60,  65]},
    {"dimensionValues": ["Redwood", "GCP"], "budgetAmounts": [100, 115, 120]}
  ]
}
```

Since each segment is "assigned" to a billing center, different users will only see segments that they have access to:
- A user that doesn't have access to "Oaktree" or "Redwood" billing centers will not be able to see anything in the report.
- A user with access only to "Oaktree" will see just the first two segments in the report.
- A user with access only to "Redwood" will see only the last two segments in the report.
- A user with org-level access will see all of the segments, since they have access to both "Oaktree" and "Redwood".

## Budget JSON Editor UI

There is a prototype, standalone tool for editing budget JSON. It provides an interactive UI that enables you to visualize, edit, and validate budget JSON data:

- [Budget JSON Editor UI](https://s3-us-west-1.amazonaws.com/rs-api-docs/bill_analysis/budget_json_editor/index.html)

Features:

- **Two-way editing**: The editor displays the budget JSON on the left side and an editable UI representation on the right side. Changes made in either view are automatically reflected in the other.

- **Spreadsheet integration**: You can copy the budget table to a spreadsheet or paste content from a spreadsheet, making it easy to convert between formats.

- **Local validation**: The JSON data is validated locally in the browser, ensuring compatibility with the budget API.

## Budget Reports
The API also includes a powerful "Report" action, which allows you to generate a detailed report comparing your budget, forecast with actual spend. The report can be filtered by date range, aggregated across dimensions, and even include unbudgeted spend to identify new costs not covered by your existing budget.

For more information, please refer to the description for the `budgets/{id}/report` action, below.
tags.name: Budget

The capabilities granted to an org determine the functionality the org has access to.

For example, the 'iam' capability is always granted to every org, giving principals in that org (with appropriate roles) access to identity and access management resources and functionality.

This data comes from scraping information from the cloud vendors once per day.
For each bill connect in the org, details are gathered for its associated accounts.
The account tags may be particularly useful, as bill data does not typically include account tag information.

Currently, only bills from Amazon Web Services (AWS) are supported.

Customization Type provides organizations with a list of all available customization options for the Automation capability. These are read-only
and changes to their values can be made by interacting with the [Customization Value](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/api/policy/v1#/Customization%20Value) API.
For example, a user could look up the "policy-published-by-email" customization type here and see that it is used to describe the authors of Catalog Templates

Adding a customization value will replace the default value for your Organization and all of your [MSP Child Orgs](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/api/iam/v1#/MSP%20Customer). Removing it will do the same. All changes

IP access control enables an administrator to add an optional layer of security to their organization, 
by defining IP ranges from which principals (users or service accounts) may access the organization.

- When no rules are defined, connections from any IP address are allowed
- When at least one rule is defined, only connections explicitly allowed by a rule are permitted

Regardless of IP access control rules, principals must still authenticate with their credentials. A principal who is
denied access to an organization based on IP access control may still access other organizations they are a part of.

tags.description:
Customers that function as managed service providers (MSPs) are granted the 'msp' capability. 
The 'msp' capability grants access to the MSP Customer APIs, which enable MSPs to create, manage and delete orgs for their customers.

The MSP's org, which has been granted the 'msp' capability is commonly referred to as the MSP "parent" org.
Customer orgs provisioned by that MSP parent org are commonly referred to as "child" orgs. 
MSP child orgs may be assigned a subset of the MSP parent org's capabilities. 
Orgs provisioned through this API are immediately available and functional.

Access to MSP customer orgs is granted by the owners attribute. 
Owners specified in that list are given administrator access (the org owner role is granted) to that child org. 

There is no permission inheritance between MSP parent and child orgs. 
Capabilities and org owners must be granted and created for each customer org, respectively.
When creating and updating customer orgs, MSPs may choose to either: 
* Grant org owner access to customers within their respective organizations
* Grant org owner access to someone internal to the MSP, who will then give limited permissions to users from the MSP's customer
tags.name: MSP Customer

tags.description:
Customers that function as managed service providers (MSPs) are granted the 'msp' capability. 
The 'msp' capability grants access to the MSP Customer Domain APIs, which enable MSPs to verify identity provider domain for their customers.
tags.name: MSP Customer Domain

tags.description:
Customers that function as managed service providers (MSPs) are granted the 'msp' capability. 
The 'msp' capability grants access to the MSP Customer Tag APIs, which enable MSPs to manage tags of their customers.
tags.name: MSP Customer Tag

tags.description:
V2 API for MSP Customer operations with multi-level hierarchy support.

Customers that function as managed service providers (MSPs) are granted the 'msp' capability. 
The 'msp' capability grants access to the MSP Customer APIs, which enable MSPs to create, manage and delete orgs for their customers.

The MSP's org, which has been granted the 'msp' capability is commonly referred to as the MSP "parent" org.
Customer orgs provisioned by that MSP parent org are commonly referred to as "child" orgs. 
MSP child orgs may be assigned a subset of the MSP parent org's capabilities. 
Orgs provisioned through this API are immediately available and functional.

Access to MSP customer orgs is granted by the owners attribute. 
Owners specified in that list are given administrator access (the org owner role is granted) to that child org. 

There is no permission inheritance between MSP parent and child orgs. 
Capabilities and org owners must be granted and created for each customer org, respectively.
When creating and updating customer orgs, MSPs may choose to either: 
* Grant org owner access to customers within their respective organizations
* Grant org owner access to someone internal to the MSP, who will then give limited permissions to users from the MSP's customer

V2 API Enhancements:
* Validates MSP capability hierarchy constraints (max_depth, max_width) during create and update operations
* Returns numberOfCustomers field in all responses, showing the count of direct child organizations
* Prevents deletion of organizations that have children, ensuring safe hierarchical cleanup
* Enhanced error responses with specific error codes for hierarchy violations

These templates are used to automate compliance standards, cost management, operational tasks, security, and other repeatable tasks.
They are run by 'being applied' and creating an Applied Policy.
More information on applying a template can be found in the [Applied Policies API](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/api/policy/v1#/Applied%20Policy).

Example templates can be viewed in the [Flexera-Public Github Repository](https://github.com/flexera-public/policy_templates).
A selection of these templates are available to all users in the Automation Catalog or by querying the [Published Templates API](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/api/policy/v1#/Published%20Template).

Users can create their own policy templates or modify exiting templates and upload them to a project in their Org.
Documentation for building these templates can be found at [Policy Template Language Documentation](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Automation/PTL.htm).
Once a template is ready for testing, it can be [uploaded to Flexera One](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Automation/CreateCustomPolicy.htm#automationrefinfo_2830531361_1243084).

Policy templates **must have unique names** in the project they are uploaded in.
The name of a policy template is inside the [metadata section](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Automation/Metadata.htm).

Policy Templates can be applied ONLY in the project where they were uploaded. When a template is published in the Automation Catalog, other projects in the organization can also apply the policy.

This will only be true for published templates from the Flexera Automation Catalog.

tags.description:
Refresh tokens are long-lived, user-owned credentials for user access to Flexera One APIs.
Refresh tokens may only be generated in the Flexera One UI.
The credential value obtained from generation in the UI is sensitive, and must be stored securely as it will not be available again.
Refresh token Ids, used to reference specific refresh tokens in these APIs, are distinct from the sensitive credential obtained when the token is generated.
Users should securely retain their own refresh tokens; refresh tokens should never be shared, or stored in locations where they are accessible to other users.

A refresh token is used to generate short-lived access tokens; access tokens must be included in requests to Flexera One APIs for authentication.
Each refresh token belongs to the user who generates it, and can be used to access any resource in any org where the generating user has permission.

For security, refresh tokens that remain unused for one year will be automatically revoked.
The refresh token's expiresAt attribute indicates when the refresh token will be automatically revoked.
Each time the refresh token is used to generate an access token, the expiresAt attribute is updated to be one year in the future.
tags.name: Refresh Token

tags.description:
Report Subscriptions schedule a dashboard to be rendered to PDF and emailed to a set of recipients on a recurring cadence (daily, weekly, or monthly) at a wall-clock time in a given IANA timezone. This lets stakeholders receive a cost or usage dashboard on a schedule without logging in.

Subscriptions are organization-scoped and owned by their creator, which is derived from the JWT subject claim. Each subscription is either private (visible only to its owner) or shared (visible to other users in the organization); creating, updating, and deleting a subscription is restricted to its owner. Updates and deletes support optimistic concurrency through ETag / If-Match, so a stale write is rejected with 412 Precondition Failed.

The roles available in an org are determined by the capabilities granted to the org.

See [Flexera One Roles](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Administration/flexeraroles.htm) for a complete breakdown of the roles available in Flexera One.

tags.description:
See: [https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Optima/OptimaRuleBasedDimensions.htm](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Optima/OptimaRuleBasedDimensions.htm)

This API lets you create new dimensions that will be populated according to rules you define.
You can use these new dimensions to look at your costs from new, meaningful perspectives.

A common use case is to create several dimensions like **Department** or **Environment**, populated based on known account values.
You might define a **Department** rule-based dimension with a rule for each known account.
For instance, a rule might express: "If the account is 'aws-123', then use the value 'Finance'".
In that way, all the "aws-123" costs will be classified as being in the "Finance" Department.

## API

There are four paths for managing rule-based dimensions, under `/finops-customizations/v1/orgs/{orgId}`:
  - `/rule-based-dimensions`: List all rule-based dimensions.
  - `/rule-based-dimensions/{id}`: Show, create, update, delete a single rule-based dimension.
  - `/rule-based-dimensions/{id}/summary`: Show a summary of distinct rule values and rule-list links.
  - `/rule-based-dimensions/{id}/rules/{effectiveAt}`: Show, replace, delete a single rules list.

Each rule-based dimension has an `id` and a display `name`.
It can also have rule lists describing how to populate the dimension over time.

There is a prototype rules list UI where you can paste in JSON on the left and view/edit a human-readable version on the right:
- [Rule List JSON Editor](https://reference.rightscale.com/bill_analysis/rbd_json_editor/index.html)

### Rule List

A rule list describes how a rule-based dimension should be populated.
A rule simply has a `condition` and a `value`.
As each line of your bill data is gathered, the rules will be evaluated in order and the first rule to match will determine the value to populate for that row.

The `value` field can specify either:
- A static text value (using `text`), or
- A dynamic value from another dimension (using `dimension`). 
        
Here are example rules demonstrating different `value` configurations:

#### Example 1: Static Text Value
This rule says: if the vendor account is AWS, populate the rule-based dimension with the static value "Finance":
~~~~
{
 "condition": {
   "type":      "dimension_equals",
   "dimension": "vendor",
   "value":     "AWS"
 },
 "value": {
   "text": "Finance"
 }
}
~~~~
The next rule demonstrates a dimension_contains condition.

The rule says: If a resource type contains the substring "Compute", populate the rule-based dimension with the value "Finance":
~~~~
{
 "condition": {
   "type":      "dimension_contains",
   "dimension": "resource_type",
   "substring": "Compute"
 },
 "value": {
   "text": "Finance"
 }
}
~~~~
If you're populating a dimension based on 100 different accounts, your rules list might have 100 rules similar to that one, specifying the value to use for each of the 100 accounts.

#### Example 2: Dynamic Dimension Value
This rule says: if the "tag_department" is not empty or "None", populate the rule-based dimension with the value of the "tag_department":
~~~~
{
  "condition": {
    "type": "not",
    "expression": {
      "type": "or",
      "expressions": [
        {
          "type": "dimension_equals",
          "dimension": "tag_department",
          "value": "None",
          "caseInsensitive": false
        },
        {
          "type": "dimension_equals",
          "dimension": "tag_department",
          "value": ""
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "value": {
    "dimension":  "tag_department",
  }
}
~~~~

#### Rule Condition

A rule's condition could be:
- The `dimension_equals` or `dimension_contains` type
- A boolean operator type: `and`, `or`, `not`
- Empty (null), meaning the rule will match unconditionally

A `dimension_equals` condition checks whether a dimension equals a certain value and a `dimension_contains` condition checks whether a dimension contains a certain substring.
Most dimensions are available to be referenced:
- Default dimensions:
  - `availability_zone`
  - `bill_entity`
  - `bill_source`
  - `billing_account`
  - `commitment_id`
  - `commitment_name`
  - `database_edition`
  - `database_engine`
  - `deployment_option`
  - `description`
  - `instance_type`
  - `instance_type_family`
  - `invoice_id`
  - `license_model`
  - `line_item_type`
  - `manufacturer_name`
  - `meter_category`
  - `operating_system`
  - `product_order_name`
  - `purchase_option`
  - `region`
  - `resource_group`
  - `resource_type`
  - `service`
  - `service_family`
  - `usage_type`
  - `usage_unit`
  - `vendor`
  - `vendor_account`
  - `vendor_account_name`
- Any custom tag dimensions
- Any other rule-based dimensions (as long as the reference doesn't create a circular dependency among the rule-based dimensions)

By default, the condition is case-sensitive, but it can be made case-insensitive by setting its `caseInsensitive` field to `true`.
This applies to both  "dimension_equals" and "dimension_contains"  condition types.
For example:

~~~~
{
  "type": "dimension_equals",
  "dimension": "vendor",
  "value": "AWS",
  "caseInsensitive": true
}
~~~~

A rule's condition could also be more complex, using the boolean operators `and`, `or`, or `not` to build a larger, nested expression.
For example:

_"vendor is AWS **and** service is EC2":_
~~~~
{
 "type": "and",
 "expressions": [
   {"type":"dimension_equals", "dimension":"vendor",  "value":"AWS"},
   {"type":"dimension_equals", "dimension":"service", "value":"EC2"}
 ]
}
~~~~

_"vendor is **not** Azure":_
~~~~
{
 "type": "not",
 "expression": {
   "type":"dimension_equals", "dimension":"vendor", "value":"Azure"
 }
}
~~~~

Rule conditions must use the underlying cost dimension values, not UI display labels.
Some UI surfaces show friendlier names for display.
For example, the displayed vendor name "Google" may correspond to the underlying vendor value "GCP", which is the value the rule must use.
If a dimension is not offered as a dropdown in the rule editor, inspect your cost data to determine the exact raw values present in your org.

### Rules can change over time
The rules for a rule-based dimension are able to change over various time periods — you could define a fresh rules list for each calendar month, if desired.

Each rules list has an `effectiveAt` date, indicating the year-month when the list starts being applicable. 
It remains in effect until a new rules list is added with a subsequent `effectiveAt` date.

For example, a rules list might take effect in "2022-01" (January). Those rules remain in effect from that month forward, until another rules list is defined for a subsequent month.
You might then add a rules list effective "2023-04" (April) and those rules would then be used for that month forward.

### Quotas
An org may define up to 50 rule-based dimensions. And each dimension may define up to 48 rules lists, meaning the rules list can change over time (at 48 unique "effectiveAt" dates).

A rules list normally supports up to 500 rules.
To limit the complexity of the condition expressions, there may be 1,000 plain condition elements (whether of type "dimension_equals", "dimension_contains", "and", "or", or "not") used across the entire list after mapping optimization. That means a list might have 500 simple "dimension_equals"/"dimension_contains" rules, or on the other extreme, might only be allowed to have one rule if that rule contains 1,000 condition elements (for example, a large "or" expression with 999 "dimension_equals" checks).

#### Special Case
There is also a special case on the number of rules: if a list consists of rules that simply check the value of the same dimension (or set of dimensions), we can optimize that and can allow up to 40,000 raw rules in that list, as long as the optimized representation has no more than 500 rule groups.

A common use case would be to populate a rule-based dimension entirely based on the value of the "vendor_account" dimension.
For instance, you might know the "Department" that should be assigned for every possible account value.
The rules list could support mapping up to 40,000 "vendor_account" values that exist in the org, following this format:
~~~
"rules": [
 {
   "condition": {"type":"dimension_equals", "dimension":"vendor_account", "value":"account_1"},
   "value": {"text": "Finance"}
 },
 {
   "condition": {"type":"dimension_equals", "dimension":"vendor_account", "value":"account_2"},
   "value": {"text": "Engineering"}
 },
 ...<up to 39,998 more rules like the two above>...
]
~~~
This same optimization also applies for rules that check the value of multiple dimensions.
As long as each rule consists of an `and` expression that checks the value of up to 6 dimensions, we can optimize that mapping and support up to 40,000 rules in that list.
Each of those rules must be checking the same set of dimensions, for example all the rules might check both the "vendor_account" and "resource_group" dimensions.

Across all rule-based dimensions, a single effective month may have up to 400,000 applicable raw rules in total, and up to 2,000 optimized rule groups after mapping optimization.
## Rule-Based Dimension for Billing Center Allocation

This section outlines the use of a special rule-based dimension, `rbd_bc`, as a powerful alternative to traditional [billing center allocation rules](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Optima/Allocation_Rules.htm).

### Advantages of `rbd_bc`

Compared to traditional allocation rules, using `rbd_bc` provides the following benefits:
- Enables the rules to change over time, allowing a different rules list for each month.
- Provides the ability to reference other dimensions that are unavailable to traditional allocation rules, such as other rule-based dimensions, custom tag dimensions, and most built-in dimensions.
- Simplifies the allocation process because one rules list directly assigns costs to leaf-node billing centers, whereas traditional allocation rules require separate rules lists at each level of the hierarchy.

### How to Use `rbd_bc`

To use `rbd_bc` for billing center allocation, follow these steps:

1. Create a rule-based dimension `rbd_bc` which will take over assigning billing center allocations.
   - The `id` must be `rbd_bc`.
   - The `name` can be anything, like "BC", or "Assign to BC", etc. Like any other rule-based dimension, it will be visible in the UI.
1. Choose an `effectiveAt` date for the first rules list. This controls a one-way switchover: starting on that date, the traditional billing center allocation rules will be overridden by this rule-based dimension’s assignments.
1. Create a rules lists that assign costs to a "leaf-node" billing center ID, for example:

       IF vendor_account = "account1" THEN "bc123"

   The end result is that `rbd_bc` will be populated with the ID of the billing center to assign to.
   And the billing center should be a leaf node in the hierarchy, allowing you to freely assign to a billing center several layers down.

#### Example `rbd_bc` Configuration

Here’s an example configuration to create the `rbd_bc` dimension:
~~~
{
  "id": "rbd_bc",
  "name": "Assign to BC"
}
~~~
And we might create a rules list effective `2023-01`, with two rules that assign an account to a specific billing center
(this rules list can be pasted into the [prototype editor UI](https://reference.rightscale.com/bill_analysis/rbd_json_editor/index.html) for further editing):
~~~
[
  {
    "condition": {
      "type": "dimension_equals",
      "dimension": "vendor_account",
      "value": "798380790996"
    },
    "value": {
      "text": "dmsP6WK7qL6yiluIl_3iOQ"
    }
  },
  {
    "condition": {
      "type": "dimension_equals",
      "dimension": "vendor_account",
      "value": "594348054263"
    },
    "value": {
      "text": "YbPKQSkO_qoE6hJ8nx9vkg"
    }
  }
]
~~~
The next time costs are imported, the billing center assignments will be driven by the `rbd_bc` values, starting on its earliest effectiveAt date (`2023-01` in this example).
The traditional billing center allocation rules will only affect dates before this `rbd_bc` effectiveAt date.

### `rbd_bc` for Recommendations

The `rbd_bc` dimension will also override billing center allocation on [savings recommendations](https://docs.flexera.com/flexeraone/EN/WhatsNew/FeatureList/CCORecommendations.htm). This works by internally populating the rule-based dimensions (RBDs) on each recommendation and using the `rbd_bc` value to allocate the recommendation to a billing center.

However, recommendations are separate from cost data and only have two fields available for RBD rules to reference:
- `vendor_account`
- `resource_group`

Any RBD rules checking the recommendation's account or resource group should work, for example:
- `IF vendor_account == "A" THEN "bc123"`
- `IF resource_group == "B" THEN "bc456"`

If an RBD rule checks the value of an unsupported dimension, such as `bill_source == "X"`, that clause will evaluate to false because the recommendation doesn't have a `bill_source` field.

But a rule containing an unsupported dimension could still match if it contained an `OR` expression.
Consider the following example rule condition that checks two fields:
```
bill_source == "X" OR vendor_account == "A"
```

Since `bill_source` doesn't exist on recommendations, the `bill_source == "X"` clause evaluates to false. However, the overall rule can still match if `vendor_account == "A"`.

To verify a domain for an identity provider, first register the domain to get a verificationCode.
After the verificationCode's value is added to the domain host’s DNS records, the domain should be verified via the "verify" endpoint, which completes verification for that domain.

See [Adding a Domain](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Administration/AddDomain.htm) and [Verifying a Domain with a TXT Record](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Administration/VerifyDomain.htm) for more detail.
tags.name: SAML2 Domain

tags.description:
SAML2 identity providers (IdP) enable SAML2-based single sign-on (SSO), which allows users to authenticate to Flexera One through an external identity provider (instead of a password).
Both the IdP in Flexera and the external identity provider must be configured with parameters from the other party.
An IdP must also have at least one domain verified to successfully authenticate users into Flexera One.

Refer to [Identity Provider Configuration](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Administration/IDPConfig.htm) for detailed guides on configuring SSO.
tags.name: SAML2 Identity Provider

tags.description:
Each SAML2 Identity Provider may have multiple signing keys.
Exactly one signing key is active at a time; the IdP's requestSigningKeyId attribute indicates the Id of the active signing key.

When the IdP's signAuthnRequests attribute is true, the active signing key is used to sign the SAML2 AuthNRequest (request sent by Flexera to the external identity provider, requesting to authenticate a user).
The signing key should be stored by the external identity provider to validate the signature included in the AuthNRequest.
Validating this signature confirms that the AuthNRequest was sent by Flexera One, and has not been modified.

Signing keys are valid for a fixed period of time, specified when they are generated.
Rotating signing keys involves generating a new signing key, updating the IdP's requestSigningKeyId to refer to the new signing key's Id, then updating the signing key stored by the external identity provider.
tags.name: SAML2 Identity Provider Signing Key

tags.description:
A service account is an account used by an application to access Flexera One APIs.
Users calling Flexera One APIs should use a refresh token; service account credentials should by used by machines/applications.

Service accounts, like users, must be assigned roles in an org to access resources within that org.
Service accounts may only be assigned roles in the org they were created in, and therefore may only access resources in that org.
tags.name: Service Account

tags.description:
Each service account client belongs to a service account, and consists of a clientId and clientSecret.
The clientSecret is a sensitive credential and must be stored securely.
Lost or compromised clients should be deleted immediately. 

Generally, only one of the service account's clients should be in use at a time.
The exception is during a no-downtime credential rotation, a new client must be generated and supplied to the running application acting as a service account, before the previous client is deleted. 

The service account client's clientId and clientSecret are used to authenticate with Flexera One's API.
After authentication, the application's permission in the Flexera One API is determined by the roles assigned to the service account.
tags.name: Service Account Client

tags.description:
Shared cost rules let you redistribute a set of costs across multiple destinations
based on configurable allocation strategies such as equal splits, fixed-percentage splits, or
usage-based proportional splits.
Rules are evaluated in priority order (lowest priority number first). Each rule identifies
source costs via dimensions (FOCUS dimensions, custom dimensions) and
distributes them to one or more destination dimension values.
Processing unit: allocations are applied in isolation per bill connect and per bill month.
Rules do not allocate costs across different bill connects or across different bill months.
tags.name: Shared Cost Rules

tags.description:
The Tag Dimensions APIs allow any resource tags (or "labels" in Google Cloud Platform) in your bill data to be enabled
as custom dimensions, which helps in grouping resources and analyzing the cloud bill data.

This API exposes methods to create, read, update and delete tag dimensions.

See
[Tag Dimensions](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Optima/CustomCostDimensions.htm)
for more details.

A tag dimension derives its value from specific resource tags.

However, resources might not always be consistently tagged.
For instance, while one set of resources might use the tag `"env"`, another might use `"environment"`.
To handle such inconsistencies, a tag dimension offers flexibility, supporting multiple tag keys.

In this case, by creating an `Environment` tag dimension that lists both `"env"` and `"environment"` tag keys,
the system will extract values from either of these tags to populate the `Environment` dimension,
ensuring comprehensive coverage irrespective of the tagging variations.
And if a resource has multiple matching tags, the value from the earliest listed tag key will be given precedence.

This tag dimension configuration applies to all bill months.
Any changes to the configuration will be reflected in all billing data, past and present, within 24 hours.
tags.name: Tag Dimension

tags.description:
Uses graphql to query Flexera's Unified Object Model, accessing data from various domains.

## GraphQL Syntax

### Parameters for root level fields:
- limit: maximum number of records to return.
- offset: skip number of records.
- order: sort order (ASC or DESC).

### Parameters for nested arrays:
- order: sort order (ASC or DESC).

### Directives for fields:
- @include(if: Boolean!): include the field in results if true. This is a built-in GraphQL directive.
- @skip(if: Boolean!): exclude the field in results if true. This is a built-in GraphQL directive.
- @require(if: Boolean): field and all parent fields must be non-null and contain at least one element (if array). This is a custom directive that is useful to enforce the equivalent of INNER JOIN instead of LEFT OUTER JOIN default behaviour for relationships, or as a simple filter to ensure a field value contains data.
- @flatten(if: Boolean): nested fields are flattened to the top level. Nested arrays cause higher-level fields to be denormalized, similar to a JOIN in SQL.

## Output Format

By default, the output for GraphQL is JSON. However, the API supports the following formats, which can be selected by setting the Accept HTTP header:
- application/json
- application/jsonl
- text/csv

In addition, output can be compressed by setting the Accept-Encoding HTTP header to: "gzip"
tags.name: graphql
